entities.name: PtlH
observations: Exact 339-residue sequence match to curated Bordetella pertussis PtlH (UniProt Q7VSX3) and Bordetella parapertussis homolog Q7W2T7.
PtlH is an ATPase component of the type IV secretion system required for export of assembled pertussis toxin.
Sequence contains a P-loop NTP-binding motif around residues 160–170, consistent with ATP hydrolysis.
Curated reference annotation assigns EC 7.4.2.8 and protein-exporting ATPase activity.
Reference mutagenesis indicates residues 175–176 are important for ATPase activity and pertussis-toxin secretion.

entities.name: ATP hydrolysis for protein export
observations: PtlH catalyzes ATP + H2O → ADP + phosphate, coupled to energy-dependent export of a cellular protein through the type IV secretion system.
The generic hydrolysis equation is directly supported by the curated PtlH annotation; coupling to protein export is a biological role rather than a covalent substrate transformation by PtlH.

entities.name: Bordetella type IV secretion
observations: PtlH is a peripheral inner-membrane, cytoplasmic-side component of the Ptl type IV secretion system.
The system uses PtlH ATPase activity as a molecular motor for secretion of assembled pertussis toxin.
